messages:
alex.dev: Quick proposal — we should try a sticky-session aware drain for preemptible nodes to avoid token-stream cutovers and downstream 5xx spikes. Idea: keep active streaming sessions on node until their KV-cache seq completes (short grace), but stop accepting new sessions and requeue short-running non-streaming requests.

maria_hw: +1. can you sketch config? how long is "short grace"? we need bounds for SLO math.

alex.dev: Thinking: grace_seconds = 30 for active streams (finish current chunk), requeue_window_ms = 5000 for in-flight requests, and a hardDrain after 90s. Also prefer local replay for token streams instead of immediate cutover.

tyler_ops: Curious about requeue semantics — if we requeue to different node, how do we avoid duplicate completions on client side? we currently rely on idempotency tokens but streaming complicates that.

alex.dev: Good point. Plan: for streaming requests we emit a brief "handoff frame" that gives client a resume token. If resume accepted, new node continues KV cache from checkpoint. Fallback: if client doesn't resume within requeue_window_ms we re-run full request but mark as retry so clients can de-dupe. Example frame: 
```
{ "handoff": true, "resume_token": "r-<node>-<seq>", "expires_ms": 5000 }
```

sam_sre: Any perf numbers? will this increase tail latency because we wait to finish streams on draining nodes?

alex.dev: Minimal. We only keep streams that are actively emitting within last chunk interval (~20-40ms). Most streams idle for >1s between tokens so they get cutover. For long-running streams (LLMs with streaming responses), we let them finish current chunk; this reduces broken streams and user-visible errors. Overall SLO hit <0.5% additional latency for handoff cases in our sim.

maria_hw: I like it. Can we gate by pool type? e.g., only enable sticky drain on mixed-capacity pools where preemptible evictions are frequent, and disable on dedicated nodes to avoid extra complexity.

tyler_ops: Also need to instrument metrics: drain.sticky.applied, drain.requeued.count, handoff.resume.success, handoff.resume.latency. add a tracing tag with node_id and eviction_id.

alex.dev: Agreed. Proposed config snippet for k8s daemon (pseudoconfig):
```yaml
drainPolicy:
  stickySessions: true
  graceSeconds: 30
  hardDrainAfterSeconds: 90
  requeueWindowMs: 5000
  enableOnPools: ["mixed-spot","mixed-preemptible"]
  resumeTokenTTLMs: 5000
```

infra-bot: deploy-bot: will schedule a canary rollout of sticky-drain v0.2 to mixed-spot pool (5% nodes) at 07:10 UTC.

sam_sre: For rollback plan, if we see >=3% spike in 5xx or handoff.resume.success < 60% for 10m, auto-disable stickySessions cluster-wide. Also watch cost delta — if sticky keeps sessions on preemptible longer it could reduce evictions but might raise transient GPU-hours.

maria_hw: Let's add a cheap simulation run against last 7 days of eviction traces before canary. Can we simulate resume token loss rates?

alex.dev: Yep, I can run a sim this afternoon. I'll also add a small experiment: instrument a header from client that prefers resumable streams vs non-resumable; use that to prioritize handoff only when client supports it.

tyler_ops: One more ops note: ensure kube-proxy / node network teardown doesn't drop in-flight TCP so we don't corrupt streaming frames. Add a pre-drain iptables rule to delay teardown for active sessions.

alex.dev: noted. I'll include a deployment checklist:
- canary sim results attached
- metrics & alerts
- resume token schema + client SDK changes
- pre-drain network hold script
- rollback automated flag

maria_hw: Thanks. @alex.dev please post sim results here and tag infra-bot when canary scheduled.

alex.dev: Will do. Starting sim now. :hourglass:
